headline: Referred Walmart Depot plan at 440 Highland Avenue to Design Review Board; approved hotel plan at 11 Summer Street with conditions.
summary: Approved a renovation of 11 Summer Street to add a 16-unit hotel, with conditions, and changes to a site plan at 160 Federal Street. Continued the Walmart Depot plan at 440 Highland Avenue and the car wash plan at 370 to 382 Highland Avenue to December 17, 2026.
decisions: Referred the Walmart Depot site plan at 440 Highland Avenue to the Design Review Board, 8-0.
Continued the Walmart Depot site plan at 440 Highland Avenue to December 17, 2026, 8-0.
Approved the site plan with conditions for the hotel renovation at 11 Summer Street, 8-0.
Continued the car wash site plan at 370 to 382 Highland Avenue to December 17, 2026, 8-0.
Approved the decision on the site plan at 160 Federal Street, 8-0.
Declined to nominate a Planning Board member to the Design Review Board, 8-0.
Approved the minutes from September 17, October 15, and October 19, 2026, 8-0.
Continued the November 5, 2026 meeting minutes to December 3, 2026, 8-0.

City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes November 19, 2026 
Page 1 of 12 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028

MEETING AGENDA 
A public hearing for the Salem Planning Board was held on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 
6:30 p.m. via remote access. Public participation was possible via Zoom video and conference 
call. 
 
Chair Kirt Rieder calls the meeting to order at 6:30 pm 
I. ROLL CALL  
Present: Chair Kirt Rieder, Vice Chair Sarah Tarbet, Jonathan Berk, Zach Caunter, Elena 
Eimert, Tom Furey, Josh Turiel, and Graham Wing (8) 
Absent: Helen Sides (1) 
Arriving Late: (0) 
Leaving Early: (0) 
Also in attendance: Claudia Cunningham, Planner 
 
II. REGULAR AGENDA 
 
A. 440 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 4)  
Applicant: Kinetic Design and Development f/b/o Walmart  
Description: A continuation of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Kinetic Design & Development F/b/o Walmart located at 440 
Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 4) in the Business Park Development District (BPD) 
and Entrance Corridor Overlay District (ECOD) for Site Plan Review and Business 
Park Development Special Permit in accordance with Section 9.5 Site Plan 
Review and Section 8.3 Business Park Development District of the Salem Zoning 
Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant proposes to internally renovate and repair 
the vacant storefronts in the plaza to move their “Spark” program Depot from 
the existing Walmart. No changes to the building footprint are proposed.  
 
Steve Martorano, Bohler Engineering, is in attendance for the applicant. 
Walmart is proposing “The Depot,” an online grocery and household items store. 
This is façade and entry improvements only, with special permit required for the 
new use. The footprint stays the same, eleven thousand seven hundred and 
 
CITY OF SALEM
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes November 19, 2026 
Page 2 of 12 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
thirty (11,730) square feet with one hundred and sixty three (163) parking 
spaces. The façade will be cleaned up and there is no branding, There will be 
wayfinding to help the drivers find the location. This location is for online orders 
to be delivered to customers; it is not open to the public though the interior will 
be similar to a typical grocery store. This is essentially happening on site today, 
but this new facility will be more efficient. Traffic is lower than at a typical retail 
plaza. There is an added Community Benefit as food close to expiration is 
donated to Feeding America. 
Public Comment 
None 
Planning Board Comments 
Mr. Furey is  glad Walmart is staying in Salem and is investing in Salem. Asks if 
they have met with the neighbors in Ward 4 or the councilor? This is like a Super 
Walmart and they should be reassessed. Mr. Martorano says no one has spoken 
with Councilor Flynn, but they would be happy to do so.  
Mr. Turiel sees this as a minor change of use. Doesn’t see why this has to go on. 
Ms. Eimert appreciates that this is a portion of an existing commercial use but 
thinks that the aerial demonstrates that this is out of alignment with the city’s 
expectation of an ECOD property, particularly regarding landscaping and curbing. 
There are requirements attached to a special permit for open space.  
Mr. Rieder asks Ms. Cunningham if the submission met the fundamental 
requirement for the drawing set; she responds in the negative. Mr. Martorano 
says that a photometric plan was shared last time. They went with one sheet as 
there are no changes proposed. They could break it out. Mr. Rieder says the best 
answer is that there are no changes planned so no plans were provided. 
Mr. Rieder asks if all the glass windows are tinted or clear; Mr. Martorano says 
tinted with twenty to thirty (20-30) percent visibility. Mr. Rieder asks where the 
truck access is on the backside. There is no dock or a proposed dock. Mr. 
Martorano says that regarding the traffic study, overall trips are a little higher 
but in the traffic study, they looked at the impact during peak hours. The Depot 
is open 6 a.m. - 11 p.m. and the traffic is steady over the entire day.  
Mr. Rieder says that he watches cars cut into the parking lot, go around the 
island and pretend there is no light at the stop light. Sympathetic to Elena’s 
comments regarding ECOD expectations and that has him asking why things on 
Highland Avenue are denuded? Why cannot be brought up to basic standards.

Mr. Martorano says they would be fine if there was a condition if there was a 
planting plan. Mr. Rieder asks what the goal is for tonight? Ms. Cunningham says 
that pers 8.2.8., the Board cannot take action until the Design Review Board 
(DRB) has provided a recommendation. The team is encouraged to look at ECOD 
requirements for frontage. 
A motion to refer the project to the Design Review Board is made my Tom Furey, seconded by 
Elena Eimert, and passes 8-0 in a roll call vote.

B. 11 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 459), 5-9 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 461), and 
15 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 462)  
Applicant: West House LLC, Emmerton House LLC, and Peabody House LLC,  
Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of West House LLC, Emmerton House LLC, and Peabody House LLC, 
all d/b/a The Salem Inn, located at 5,7,9 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 459), 11-13 
Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 461), and 15 Summer Street (Map 26, Lot 462) in 
the B5 – Central Development district and Urban Renewal Overlay for Site Plan 
Review in accordance with Section 9.5 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. 
Specifically, the applicant proposes the renovation of the existing 3 story building

at 11 Summer Street to accommodate a hotel with 16 units. The applicant is 
proposing site renovations including an increase of parking, through exterior 
parking changes, and renovations of the existing 2 story garage. Other site 
improvements include landscape improvements, and solar car ports.  
 
Dan Ricciarelli, Seger Architects, Dick Pabich, the Salem Inn, Katie Olyha Stonfield 
Engineering,  Michael Blier, Landworks Studio, Scott Grover, Tinti Navins, and  
Julia Mooradian, Seger Architects, are in attendance for the applicant.  
Ms. Olyha shares the civil plan changes. Modifications around the carriage house 
area to aid in site circulation (removal of bollards). Provided photometric plans. 
Other are utility configurations; courtyard area, overall formula is the same and 
is to create a cohesive campus.  
Mr. Blier shares the updated landscape plan. Street edge and campus. One-way 
circulation in and out. Spaces between 15 and 11 Summer Street are like a 
pocket park. This allows a continuous landscape almost to the Salem Inn. Trying 
to blend established landscape into a larger sustainable palette.  
Public Comment 
Written Public Comment 
Ana Gordan 
12 Crombie Street 
 Submitted written comment but is still concerned about construction 
disturbance. Asking that the boundary and limits of work be respected. 
Communication has been non-existent, particularly regarding construction. How 
will trash be handled? And the snow storage is insufficient for a winter like last 
year. Is excited and supportive of project, but worried about the construction 
management.  
 
Mr. Grover says that there is a lot of detail in the decision for SPR that provides 
the protection that the abutter is looking for. Regarding trash, Mr. Pabich says 
that right now it is picked up by a contractor at the entrance of 5-9 Summer 
Street and nothing will change from the current situation. Regarding  snow 
storage, there is decision language to require the applicant to remove snow from 
site if the snow storage is not sufficient.  
Planning Board Comment 
Mr. Rieder asks if there could be clarification of where the asphalt curbs v. 
vertical granite curbs (VGC) are located? Ms. Olyha only proposes granite within 
the Summer Street line; interior curbs would be asphalt. Mr. Rieder asks Ms. 
Cunningham if VGC solely in public way and a different material for the interior is

normal? Ms. Cunningham says that the Salem Redevelopment Authority (SRA) 
and DRB have done their own reviews, but only the ECOD requires granite 
curbing. Mr. Rieder says that he is disappointed in the downgrade. Mr. Rieder 
wonders if there is a way to add brick back into the corridor along 9 and 11 to 
make it more unified with the campus. Mr. Ricciarelli asks if they can do brick for 
the driveway? Mr. Pabich says the  intention is to keep the existing brick 
driveway, relaying bricks and extend to the corner of the two (2) buildings in the 
back. Mr. Rieder asks about the heat pump condensers in front and if they will  
be relocated. Mr. Pabich says it is preexisting and they are hoping to be natural 
gas free; what can they do to mitigate what is there now. Asks that they work for 
a rigid, intentional solution. Mr. Pabich says the SRA said this was a solution.  
Mr. Rieder says that at the driveway back to the carriage house there is no street 
tree at the curb cut. Would like a street tree there.  
Ms. Eimert asks if the solar carport is cantilevered; yes.  
A motion to close the public hearing is made by Josh Turiel, seconded by Jonathan Berk, and 
passes 8-0 in a roll call vote.

C. 370 376 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 63) 378 380 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 
64), 382 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 65)  
Applicant: Joseph Correnti f/b/o GR Development LLC  
Description: A continuation of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application Joseph Correnti f/b/o GR Development LLC for the property located 
at 370 376 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 63) 378 380 Highland Avenue (Map 3, 
Lot 64) and 382 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 65) in the (B2) Business Highway 
and (ECOD) Entrance Corridor Overlay District zoning districts for Site Plan 
Review in accordance with Section 9.5 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. 
Specifically, the applicant proposes to demolish two existing buildings onsite, 
"Puleo's Dairy" and a storage facility, to construct a 4,400 s.f. car wash facility. 24 
onsite parking spaces are proposed, 22 of which will also be used as vacuum 
stations.  
 
Attorney Joseph Correnti, Frank Dougherty, Washville, Bob Griffin, Griffin 
Engineering, and Scott Thornton, Vanasse and Associates are in attendance.  
Mr. Thornton says they revised the plan addressing Board and neighborhood 
concerns. They feel an entrance only from Savona Street has limited effect on 
the neighborhood and that is the plan presented. It maintains Highland Avenue 
access and eliminates the concern of traffic cutting through the site. Traffic will 
not be able to exit Savona Street. The traffic coming  from Ravenna Avenue will 
be people from the neighborhood. Traffic from north on Highland Avenue would 
right turn in and out. All traffic would have a right turn out. Coming from south 
would be able to turn left at a left turn part of the signalized intersection. Once 
on Ravenna Avenue, it is only impacted a short stretch. All traffic will exit to 
Highland Avenue. 
Mr. Griffin tried to put distinct curve into entrance area to eliminate exiting 
Savona Street. Additionally, this is a manned facility. They also twisted the 
dumpster on the pad to allow easier access for the dump truck. The DRB asked 
that the color palette be more muted. 
Landscape improvements include low-growth sumac and Boston ivy. The ECOD 
requires one (1) tree/three (3) parking spaces; eight (8) trees are required and 
twelve are provided. Honey locust has been swapped for pin oak and shrubs 
have been added on Highland Avenue as well as Japanese lilacs and red twig 
dogwoods.  
Public Comment 
Written Public Comment
City of Salem Planning Board

Scott Morgan 
7 Savona Street 
This is a residential, R1, single family street. The lots are being used as 
commercial junkyards and at 2-4 Ravenna Avenue. Appreciates the detail of 
trees, but there need to be more done on the backside, not just low levelling 
plantings. Concerned about the noise as the exit faces his home.  
 
Tim Flynn 
Ward 4 Councilor 
42 Sable Road 
Appreciates the changes to the entrance and exit, but curious to hear what the 
residents think of this. Concern is that the neighbors are happy. Has the team 
been in touch with MassDOT? Some residents are worried about the uses of 
water. Can they speak on the recycling of the water and the noise from the 
vacuums.  
 
John Harvey 
27 Ravenna Avenue 
Appreciates the entrance only off of Savona Street. Likes the idea of the car wash 
rather than a restaurant.  
 
Helen Hughes  
24 Ravenna Avenue  
Likes the revised site. Would like the team to pay attention to Scott Morgan’s 
ideas. As far as noise, are the vacuums facing Highland Avenue or are they 
limiting the number of vacuums.  
 
Mr. Dougherty on the recycling water: A four (4) stage process of recycling 
water. There are a series of sanitation tanks on the front of the building. Some 
portion is flushed to the sewer. Regarding noise, recognize the Salem noise 
ordinance. A lot of the prohibitions don’t apply to this site. Two locations for 
noise generation: the blowers are at the exit of the tunnel and the vacuums 
facing Highland Avenue. Nonstructural and structural measures in place for noise 
mitigation. Nonstructural: 1. Siting of tunnel, with exit away from homes. 2. 
There is staff on site to mitigate the non-site related noise. Structural: 1. The 
vacuums are inside the building. 2. The blowers on the outside of exit tunnel are 
“stealth dryers.” This is about ninety nine (99) percent less sound energy than a 
traditional dryer.  
Planning Board Comments
City of Salem Planning Board

Mr. Furey thinks this is a breath of fresh air from the neighborhood.  
Ms. Eimert wonders on the fence proposed on Ravenna Avenue and have they 
looked at the visibility intersection ordinance and visibility? Mr. Griffin says the 
fence is pulled back from the intersection, and it is only four (4) foot. Mr. 
Thornton says that they had a meeting with MassDOT in September, and they 
asked about changes to the intersections. They are not proposing anything 
dramatic. There will be improved bicycle and pedestrian access. Ms. Eimert asks 
if the applicant does not own property north of Savona Street. But they own no 
property. Mr. Rieder says that it is one owner for everything, but the applicant is 
a tenant.  
Mr. Correnti says the sign will be part of the agreement with the landowner for 
use of the property.  
Mr. Rieder asks if the ingress off Savona Street has to be twenty (20) feet wide or 
could it be smaller to discourage wrong way drivers. Mr. Griffin says that twenty 
(20) feet is the minimum for emergency vehicles. Mr. Rieder is curious why the 
water line orientation is it existing? Mr. Griffin says they anticipate connection to 
existing. Regarding noise, the car wash on  Canal Street has made their vacuums 
internal and it is much quieter, this should provide comfort to the neighbors. On 
landscaping, where is the Boston ivy planted; top of wall along Savona Street  
and Ravenna Avenue. Mr. Rieder suggests that Boston ivy is a climber, not a 
trailing plant. Mr. Rieder says that they have stop planting dogwoods in Eastern 
Massachusetts as they are dying. Not a fan of the two Japanese lilacs on 
Highland Avenue. Tropical Products has planted seventeen (17) trees. There are 
no overhead power lines, and he doesn’t understand the proposed trees being 
two (2) ornamental trees. Doesn’t understand the proposed concrete wall. Mr. 
Griffin says not all of the current wall will be replaced. Maybe  five to six (5-6) 
feet. There are three (3) trees there right now and two (2) of the three (3) are 
overrun. The tree hits the soil above the sidewalk. The construction of the wall 
necessitates the removal of one of the trees. The cedar wall is unpainted; and 
the fence is inside the wall is higher than ten (10) feet? It may be good to make 
the fence taller. Agrees with resident that there are insufficient trees on Savona 
Street.

D. 160 Federal Street (Map 26, Lot 2)  
Applicant: North Shore Community Development Coalition  
Description: A continuation of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of North Shore Community Development Coalition located at 160 
Federal Street (Map 26, Lot 2) in the Residential two-family (R2) district, Coastal 
Resiliency Overlay District (C-ROD), and Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD) for

III. OLD AND NEW BUSINESS 
 
A. Discuss and Vote on referring a Planning Board Member to appointment for 
the Design Review Board  
 
Ms. Tarbet is stepping down from the DRB. 
 
Ms. Cunningham says that it is up to the SRA whether there is a member of the 
Planning Board on the DRB, and it is generally acknowledged that it is helpful to 
have this arrangement but not required.  
 
Ms. Eimert asks if the benefit for the Planning Board is that there is a better 
understanding? Ms. Tarbet says that is part of it but that she tries not to speak 
for the DRB.  
 
Mr. berk says that it was helpful to have the DRB take part in joint public 
hearings and wonders if it would make sense to do more of those rather than 
having a Planning Board representative on the DRB. Mr. Rieder says that this 
makes sense. Though Ms. Cunningham reminds that it is required for a 40R 
project but there is no procedure in place for other projects.  
 
A motion to decline to nominate a member of the Planning Board to the Design Review Board is 
made by Elena Eimert, seconded by Josh Turiel, and passes 8-0 in a roll call vote.
